sub.en: Look at the sentences. When is it a, when the, and when no article at all?

items.q: I live in ___ studio flat.
items.why: a / an the first time you mention something.

items.q: ___ flat is on the fourth floor.
items.why: the when the listener knows which one you mean — usually the second time.

items.q: The building is opposite ___ garage.
It’s next to ___ Indian restaurant.
My bed is on ___ shelf above the kitchen.
I go to ___ work by bus.
items.why: No article with go to work, go home, go to bed.

items.q: She’s at ___ home this evening.
I live in ___ New York.
items.why: No article with most city and country names — but the USA and the UK keep the.

acts.title: The photo and the flat
text: THE PHOTO ON THE WEBSITE: “A bright studio flat in a modern building. Beautiful view. Quiet neighbourhood. Fourth floor. 800 a month.” There is a photo of a white room with a big window, a sofa, a carpet and long curtains. There isn’t a photo of the kitchen.

THE FLAT: “The building is opposite a 24-hour garage and next to an Indian restaurant, so there are always cars and people in the street. The cars are quite noisy. It’s a studio flat with only one room. My bed is on a shelf above the kitchen and the shower is below it. In the kitchen there’s a fridge and a cooker, but there isn’t an oven. I love it anyway — the view really is beautiful.”

write.q: Describe your home: 6 sentences. Say what kind of home it is, which floor, what is opposite and next to it, two things inside, and what it’s like. Watch the articles.
write.model: I live in a flat on the seventh floor of a modern building. The building is opposite a small park and next to a chemist. There’s a big living room with a sofa and two armchairs, and there’s a shelf above the kitchen door. There isn’t a dining room — we eat in the kitchen. It’s small, but it’s bright and very cosy.

speak.q: Answer out loud: Where do you live? Which floor? What’s opposite your building? Do you share with anybody? What’s the best thing about it?
speak.model: I live in a studio flat on the fourth floor. The building is opposite a garage, so it’s a bit noisy. I share it with my sister. The best thing is the view — you can see the mountains.
